title: Request records posted by a wake row are stranded under the wake's own id (records-sum read would drop them)
description:
Repo: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour). Found by LIN-4200 (piece 3 of LIN-4195), the re-review comment on LIN-4200.

## Problem

Request records posted by a `kind:'wake'` dispatch row before that row's first tagged feedback are stamped with the wake row's **own id** as their anchor. Once the row is later re-pointed to its lineage root, no member row carries that anchor, so the records are stranded. `RequestUsageStore.listForAnchors` (the loader piece 4 / LIN-4201 will use) never returns them.

Live evidence (LIN-4195 comment `0beba2a2-4378-4ee6-a46a-d5f1291b59ec`): 3 of 3,326 request records in the 30-day window sit under anchors that no dispatch row carries. The anchors are `89729833-f40c-4503-aa18-353ec5b4eb8c`, `2e2844c3-4a25-44ca-a4c9-8e1331ddb8ff` and `df89daf5-665a-4a13-b79f-3ceb2f39d11a`. All three are `kind:'wake'` rows of autopilot `88f03588-6670-4566-ad6c-75d04c6b6fb5` (LIN-4196); each has `followUpTo` = that autopilot. Their records were posted 08:10:46 to 08:11:18Z on 2026-11-04, while each wake ran. Proxy reads of the three rows show their tagged feedback now carries `rootItemId` = `88f03588`.

## Mechanism (from the LIN-4200 re-review; read the code to verify)

* `addItem` gives a wake row `rootItemId = its own _id`; it skips the factory's inheritance.
* `addFeedback` latches the producer's `rootItemId` onto the doc on the first tagged feedback (`update.$set = { rootItemId }`, `lib/dispatch-store.js` around L3270).
* `runOf` (around L320 of the same file) documents the caveat: a wake row's doc `rootItemId` "is never trusted for a wake".
* The usage intake ignores that caveat: `readTakenForUsage` and `anchorOf(row)` (`lib/request-usage-intake.js` around L166) stamp each record with the anchor the row has at post time.

## Why it matters

Piece 4 (LIN-4201) sums request records by anchor. Records stranded under a wake's own id are dropped from the sum, so cost is under-reported for any lineage that uses wakes. It is the first of two reasons for the NO-GO on piece 4 recorded on LIN-4195. The class is: any record posted while its row's doc `rootItemId` still differs from the value it is later latched to. Wake rows are the known instance.

## Not yet confirmed

LIN-4200's close-out could not read the three rows' document-level `rootItemId` or the order of first tagged feedback against each record's `updatedAt`; the proxy does not expose them and no read-only database credential was available. Confirm both with a read-only find on `dispatch-history` before relying on the mechanism above.
Expected if the mechanism holds: doc `rootItemId` = `88f03588...` (not the row's own id), and first tagged feedback later than the record's `updatedAt`.
If a doc `rootItemId` is still the row's own id, the lineage was dropped by `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs` instead, and that is a script defect.

## Acceptance

* Zero orphan request records in a re-measured window, using `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs` (merged with LIN-4200 PR #2267, merge commit `230cc2c2`). Its `orphanAnchors` count must be 0.
* A test that posts usage from a wake row before its first tagged feedback and shows the record is returned by `listForAnchors` for the lineage root. It must fail on the pre-fix code.
* Records already stranded (the three above, and any more found) are re-anchored or covered by a stated rule.

## Unvalidated idea

Resolve a wake through `followUpTo` at post time, as `runOf` does. Or key records on the latched root and re-key on the latch. Either would cover the whole class.

## Priority

High (priorityLevel 3): blocks LIN-4201 and under-reports cost; small today (3 of 3,326 records) but every wake that posts before its first feedback can hit it.

## Ruling (2026-11-04)

Fix shape decided (`lin4212-record-lineage-rule`): **read records by the posting row** (option F, built as F′: `listForAnchors` resolves member rows itself, reads by `itemId`, one record per `requestId`; no migration). Full plan: comment "Final investigation proposal" (`d215e60d`).

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out (2026-11-04). The full plan (draft 3 of 3, with the places table, witnesses W1-W16, boundaries and risks) is preserved in the task snapshots (pre-prune snapshot* `49497c3c`*) and the comment trail.*

**Implemented:** PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2272](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2272>), merged as `eb44eff97d6143576ba7ec2cb2c135a435a58a69` (head `5fd1397b`), deployed to `Harbour / production` 2026-11-04T11:12Z. The plan was implemented as approved (F′: `listForAnchors` resolves member rows from `dispatch-history`, reads records by posting-row `itemId`, relabels to the row's current anchor, one record per `requestId`; no migration). One recorded deviation, accepted in review: `updatedAt` stays in `LIST_PROJECTION` for the measure script's post-time coverage. One doc-only fix after approval (`5fd1397b`).

**Left out, tracked elsewhere:** runner tagging of cold-resume posts and phantom lineages: LIN-4216. Retiring the unread `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index: LIN-4217. Live re-measure, production index check and production timing: operator steps under LIN-4201's gate (see the Close-out comment).

### Session fit and review

fits one session

comments.body:
## Beat 1/4: grounded and reproduced (investigation, nothing shipped)

**HEAD:** LinearViewer `main` = `origin/main` = `230cc2c2`. There are no commits after the ticket was created (2026-11-04T08:45:48Z) on any named path. Last touches: `dispatch-store.js`, `request-usage-intake.js` and `request-usage-store.js` in `9cc5ff9c` (LIN-4198); `lineage-membership.js` in `46b43b3b`; `dispatch-wake.js` in `7797c306`; the measure script in `230cc2c2`.

### Lifecycle at HEAD
1. **Wake minted with its own id as root.** `buildWakeFollowUp` (`lib/dispatch-wake.js:169`) returns `followUpTo: sessionId` (`:218`) and **no `rootItemId`**. `_mintWake` calls `addItem` directly (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3144`), not the factory, so `doc.rootItemId = item.rootItemId || doc._id` (`:745`) gives the wake's own `_id`.
2. **Usage post.** `postUsage` reads the row with `readTakenForUsage` (`lib/request-usage-intake.js:158`, then `dispatch-store.js:3177`, projection `{_id, rootItemId, issueIdentifier}` only at `:3182`, so `kind`/`followUpTo` are not even loaded). It stamps `rootItemId: anchorOf(row)` (`request-usage-intake.js:166`). `anchorOf` is `row.rootItemId || row._id` (`lib/lineage-membership.js:27-30`). Before any tagged feedback, that is **the wake's own id**.
3. **Latch.** The first runner feedback carrying `rootItemId` sets `update.$set = { rootItemId }` (`dispatch-store.js:3270`) in the same atomic update. The doc now reads R, and `anchorOf(doc)` is R.
4. **Read.** `listForAnchors` queries `{urlKey, rootItemId: {$in: anchors}}` (`lib/request-usage-store.js:178-184`). Readers pass `anchorOf(row)` = R, and no row's anchor is the wake id anymore. **The records are stranded at step 2 by `request-usage-intake.js:166`.**
5. `runOf` (`dispatch-store.js:318-331`) says a wake's doc `rootItemId` "is never trusted for a wake" and resolves it via `followUpTo`. The intake does not apply this.

### Reproduction (fails on HEAD)
`tests/unit/lin-4212-wake-records-stranded.test.js`, on branch `lin-4212-wake-record-anchor` (local commit `483cb63b`, not pushed). It runs end to end over the runner lane on real MangoDB. The worker's `[done]` mints a real wake. The runner takes the wake and posts 3 usage records, then the first tagged feedback (`rootItemId: R`), then reads `listForAnchors(R)`. Every precondition passes: the wake has `followUpTo` R and `rootItemId` equal to its own id, and the latch lands, so `anchorOf(wakeDoc)` is R. The final assertion fails:
```
AssertionError: records the wake posted must be read under its lineage root 9cbc8e62…; found 0 there and 3 stranded under the wake's own id bc02816a… 
  + []   - ['msg_wake_1','msg_wake_2','msg_wake_3']
```

### Did not match the ticket / new
- `anchorOf` is in `lib/lineage-membership.js:27`, not `request-usage-intake.js` (it is called at `:166`). The line refs `~L3270` and `~L320` hold (`runOf` is at `:329`).
- `readTakenForUsage` projects away `kind`/`followUpTo`, so a fix like `runOf` at post time also needs that projection widened.
- **Re-post after the latch splits a record.** The upsert key is `{urlKey, rootItemId, requestId}` (`request-usage-store.js:115`). A re-post of the same `requestId` after the latch (a streamed message growing) creates a **second** doc under R and leaves the first under the wake id. Seen in a throwaway variant: `[{WAKE, out:80}, {ROOT, out:90}]`. A re-anchoring fix or migration must merge by `requestId` with `$max` and must not just re-key, or it will double-count.
- Timing in the description: `df89daf5` is listed as taken at 08:11:21, but its records are listed as posted 08:10:46–08:11:18. A post requires `status:'taken'`, so those times are probably `at` (first-line time), not `updatedAt`. The record-vs-feedback ordering is still unconfirmed live.
- **The script-defect branch is mostly ruled out, by inference.** The script fetches rows by `_id ∈ anchors` (`scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs:465`) and groups taken rows by `anchorOf`. If a wake doc still had its own id as root, it would form its own lineage and its records would *not* be orphans. Orphans therefore imply the doc anchor is no longer its own id. A direct read-only find on `dispatch-history` is still not done; I have no DB credential.

## Beat 2/4 verdict: cause CONFIRMED (indirect live evidence; the direct DB read is still not done)

**Hypothesis H.** The intake stamps each record with `anchorOf(row)` at post time (`request-usage-intake.js:166`). A wake's doc anchor is its own id (`addItem` `:745`) until its first tagged feedback latches the root (`dispatch-store.js:3270`). So a record posted in that gap is stranded.

**Decisive experiment.** For each live orphan, put two things in order: the record's POST, and the first tagged feedback on that wake row. Then read the wake doc's anchor. Source of record: the runner's own oplog and session ledger (`simple-dispatcher/state/oplog.jsonl`, `sessions.json`, read-only), cross-checked against `GET /dispatch/:id`.

| wake | taken (untagged `[started]`) | first Stop `request-usage.flush` | first tagged feedback on the row | record posted (`at`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 89729833 | 08:10:49.212 | 08:10:51.492, **posted 1** | 08:10:51.556 | `msg_011CghYojTXS…` (08:10:46.091) |
| 2e2844c3 | 08:11:05.535 | 08:11:08.225, **posted 1** | 08:11:08.411 | `msg_011CghYpwyNp…` (08:11:02.320) |
| df89daf5 | 08:11:21.853 | 08:11:24.226, **posted 1** | 08:11:24.291 | `msg_011CghYrAVyG…` (08:11:18.723) |

- The runner posts usage **before** a turn's feedback by design. `hook.js:1855` flushes "once per Stop, awaited, and BEFORE this turn's feedback posts". It posts to `/api/dispatch/usage/<itemId>`, where itemId is `session.itemMetadata.itemId`, which is the wake (`request-usage-flush.js:118,166`).
- The flush counts reconcile with the session ledger: 65 + 16 = 81 keys, and there were no re-posts. That gives exactly 3 records under the 3 wake ids, 1 each, which equals the 3 measured orphans. Their `at` values (08:10:46 to 08:11:18) match the description's range exactly. That range was the record `at`, not the post time.
- Each stranded record is the *previous* turn's trailing final-text request: its line was written after that turn's Stop had read the transcript, so the wake's first Stop posted it. It belongs to the same lineage, so the lineage total is unaffected. Only the record's `itemId` is one turn late.
- **The wake docs are latched now.** `GET /dispatch/:id` merges feedback through `_collectGroupFeedback`, which queries siblings with `rootItemId == groupAnchorFor(doc)`. All three views show the 88f03588 lineage's entries. If a doc still had its own id, it would show only its own entries. The only writers of the doc field are `addItem :745` and the latch `:3270`.

**Rivals**
- **(a) Script defect: eliminated.** Fixtures run the script's real `lineageRecords` and `orphanAnchors`. With the live shape (doc latched, record under the wake id) they give 1 orphan per wake. With a doc still on its own id they give **0** orphans, because a phantom lineage forms. So 3 live orphans can only come from latched docs, and the script classifies them correctly.
- **(b) Latched before the records, with something else stamping: eliminated.** On each wake, the only posts before its flush are the dispatcher's **untagged** `[started]` and `[working] Resumed` (proxy view and oplog). There is no other writer of `rootItemId`.
- **(c) Another path: eliminated as a cause.** All three POSTs came from the Stop flush on `/api/dispatch/usage`. The proxy runner lane did not post them, and neither did reap or cancel: the reap flush at 08:11:38 came after the latch. There were no re-posts, so the live data has no split duplicates.
- **Natural control.** 4c9f079e (07:25, same autopilot, cold resume) flushed **37** records at its first Stop, but a tagged heartbeat `[stalled?] … in RESUMING` had latched it 3 s earlier (`reapers.js:333` posts to `itemMetadata.itemId` with `session.rootItemId`). None of those records were orphaned. The warm "delivered to held session" path also latches first: the dispatcher posts a tagged `[working] Session resumed…` before `[started]`.

**Scope.** I scanned every item since the 04:59 deploy whose first Stop flush posted records (133 items, 58 of them wakes). **Only these 3 wakes stranded.** The trigger is a cold resume plus at least one pending record at the first Stop plus no tagged heartbeat in between.

**Witness validity: needs changes.**
1. `orphanAnchors == 0` is **necessary, not sufficient**. A wake whose doc never latches (for example, it flushes and then dies before any tagged feedback), or a fix that drops the latch, reads 0 orphans while its records stay outside the root lineage (fixture B). A re-anchor migration that re-keys without merging by `requestId` also reads 0 while double-counting (fixture D). The acceptance should add three checks: records anchored at any `kind:'wake'` row's own `_id` = 0; duplicate `requestId` within a lineage = 0; and lineage 88f03588 gains exactly 3 records (`msg_011CghYojTXS…`, `msg_011CghYpwyNp…`, `msg_011CghYrAVyG…`).
2. The repro now runs on **both lanes**; `dispatch` is the live runner path. It adds a re-post-after-latch **guard**. On its own, the repro passes a read-union fix. Mutation checks: a read-union passes test 1 and fails the guard; resolving the wake at write time passes both. The guard passes before the fix by design. Not yet covered: a wake whose `followUpTo` is not itself the lineage root (a child autopilot or a chained follow-up). Add it when the fix is chosen.

**Not verified.** I did not read the `request-usage` docs or the wake docs directly: there is no read-only DB credential here, and I did not use the root credential (LIN-4205). The doc anchor and the record anchors are inferred from the group-merge view and the runner ledger. The scan also assumes this runner is the only producer; opencode records are not yet posted (LIN-4202).

Branch `lin-4212-wake-record-anchor`, local commits `483cb63b` and `df4bff85` (test only, not pushed). Current result: 2 fail (repro, both lanes) and 2 pass (guard).

## Beat 3/4: the class, the fix shape, the data rule (investigation only, nothing changed)

### 1. Class scan: a record stamped with an anchor that can still change
**Why the anchor moves.** The runner tags every feedback with `session.rootItemId`, which is the session's *launch* item id. It is "set once, never overwritten" (`simple-dispatcher/dispatcher.js:236-241`, used at `hook.js:140` and `reapers.js:333`). `addFeedback` copies that tag onto the doc (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3270`). So a row is exposed whenever its birth `rootItemId` differs from the launch id of the session that runs it.

| row, born by | birth anchor | can it change after a record is stamped? |
|---|---|---|
| wake, `_mintWake` → `addItem` (`dispatch-store.js:3144`, `:3576`) | own `_id` (`:745`) | **Yes, exposed (the live case).** |
| factory follow-up, anchor read OK (`dispatch-factory.js:1076`, `:720`) | `anchor.rootItemId \|\| followUpTo` | No in practice: it already equals the session's launch id. |
| factory follow-up, anchor read **faulted** (`readOrNull` at `:182` returns null) | own `_id` | **Yes, exposed** (rare, not seen live). |
| root dispatch, kickoff, worker with `sessionId` | own `_id` = launch id | No. |
| abort rows (`expandCascadeAborts` `:2780`) | own `_id` | No: they post no usage and are not members. |

**Producers.** Every flush posts to `session.itemMetadata.itemId`, which `resumeSession` repoints to the new item before launch (`dispatcher.js:336`).
- **Stop flush:** exposed (the live case).
- **`fail` flush** (`dispatcher.js:478`) **and forced `cancel` flush** (`:1175`): exposed. A wake that fails before any tagged post may never latch. That leaves a phantom lineage with 0 orphans, the witness gap from beat 2.
- **Reap flushes:** not exposed in practice. They run after a tagged `[done]`.
- **Live window since 04:59:** 295 stop and 43 reap flushes, 0 fail or cancel.
- **opencode poster** (LIN-4202, not wired yet): same intake, same exposure once wired.

**Stampers.** `request-usage-intake.js:166` → `upsertOpFor` (`request-usage-store.js:115`) is the **only** place a copy of a row's anchor is persisted. The upsert key includes `rootItemId`, which is why a re-post after the latch splits into two docs.

**Readers.**
- **Exposed:** only `listForAnchors` (`request-usage-store.js:178`). Its callers are the D13 script and, later, LIN-4201. The measure script groups records by the stamped anchor.
- **Not exposed:** everything that reads `row.rootItemId` live at read time. That is `cost-read.js:343`, `lineage-membership.js:68`, `dispatch-lineage.js:131`, `terminal-marked-task-cost.js:156`, `dispatch-lineage-status.js`, `ci-wake-sweep.js:242`, and the snapshot usage that rides each row's feedback. These follow the latch automatically. This is why snapshots do not have this bug.

### 2. Fix shapes
- **(A) Resolve the wake at post time**, the way `runOf` does: follow `followUpTo` and widen the projection at `:3182`. Probe: passes both tests.
  - No race.
  - Covers wakes only. It misses faulted-anchor follow-ups and any row where the runner's latch value differs from `followUpTo` (a session matched by `itemMetadata.itemId`, `followup.js:47`).
  - Still trusts a stored copy, and the 3 live records still need a migration.
- **(B) Re-anchor at latch time**, merging by `requestId` with `$max`. Covers any latch change.
  - It is a second-collection write in the hot `addFeedback` path, outside its atomic update.
  - It **races**: a post that read the old anchor before the latch upserts after the move and strands again. Closing that needs a re-check after the write in the intake as well.
  - Existing records are already latched, so they still need a migration.
- **(C) Read-side union** of wake ids and the root. Probe: passes the repro but **fails the re-post guard** (double count) unless it deduplicates by `requestId`.
  - It leaves the stored data wrong.
  - It does not see a phantom (never-latched) wake.
  - It is a masking compatibility rule unless stated explicitly.
- **(D) Runner tags its first post** so the latch lands before the flush. This is a two-repo change and leaves the fail/cancel paths, other producers and older runners exposed. Harbour still trusts a copy of a value that can change. Worth doing as hygiene, but it is not the fix.
- **(E) Mint the wake with the inherited root.** It changes the lineage membership of *queued* wakes (`closeLineageRows`, stopped-run cancel, group merge), which the design deliberately avoids (`runOf` caveat). Not recommended.
- **(F) Read records by the row that posted them** (recommended). Records already store the immutable `itemId` of the posting row (`request-usage-store.js:118`). A lineage's records become those posted by its member rows, resolved at read time through `anchorOf(row)` exactly as snapshots are, with one record per `requestId` (`$max`).
  - It removes the stamped value, so it fixes **every instance of the class**, with no window and no race.
  - It needs no migration. The 3 live records carry `itemId` = a wake that is now a taken member of 88f03588.
  - Records and snapshots then agree on membership by construction, which LIN-4201's records-vs-snapshots cutover needs.
  - **Probe on unmodified code: 4/4 pass**, including the re-post guard.
  - Costs: an index `{urlKey, itemId}`; add `itemId` to `LIST_PROJECTION`; the loader takes member ids instead of anchors; the D13 timing must be re-measured.

**Recommendation: F.** Keep the intake's post-time anchor only as an attribute nothing sums by. Optionally do D on the runner side.

### 3. Existing data rule
- **Under F:** no write is needed. On re-measure the witness becomes:
  - records whose `itemId` is not a taken row = 0;
  - duplicate `requestId` within a lineage = 0 after folding;
  - lineage 88f03588 gains exactly `msg_011CghYojTXS…`, `msg_011CghYpwyNp…` and `msg_011CghYrAVyG…`.
- **Under A or B:** a one-off, idempotent re-anchor.
  - Selection: records where `rootItemId` equals a row `_id` whose current `anchorOf(row)` differs. Merge into `{urlKey, anchorOf(row), requestId}` with `$max` on the growing fields, keep the earliest `at`, then delete the old doc.
  - **Dry-run first.** Expected: 3 moves into 88f03588, 0 merges, 0 records left at any wake `_id`, total unchanged, `orphanAnchors` 0.
- Nothing has been written to production.

### 4. Direction question for the owner
Should a request record's lineage be decided **at read time by the row that posted it** (as snapshots are; option F, recommended), or **stamped on the record at post time** (the current design, which then needs A or B plus a migration)?

F changes LIN-4201's "one loader is `listForAnchors`" from anchors to member rows. It also bears on the LIN-3936 note that cost attribution should be carried per call. I think a per-call *issue* tag can stay stamped, because it doesn't change after posting. The mutable lineage anchor should not be stamped.

**Not verified:** no direct DB read (no credential). F is a probe in a test copy, not an implementation. The faulted-anchor and fail/cancel paths are exposed by code reading and were not observed live. The `lineageFeedbackCount` sibling fan-out also keys on the anchor at write time; I did not dig into it, since it isn't cost.

## Autopilot run summary (stepper, 4 beats, one warm session, kind=bug investigation)

| beat | what | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1/4 | Ground at HEAD 230cc2c2, trace lifecycle, write failing repro | comment f2151097; tests/unit/lin-4212-wake-records-stranded.test.js fails on HEAD (0 under root, 3 under wake id) |
| 2/4 | Decisive experiment + rivals + witness validity | comment 0bc838bb; runner oplog shows all 3 records posted at the wake's first Stop flush, before its first tagged feedback; script-defect rival eliminated |
| 3/4 | Class scan, fix options A-F, data rule | comment ef7f44d8; only listForAnchors depends on the stamped anchor |
| 4/4 | Stress-test F, consolidate | comment d215e60d (Final investigation proposal); F' probed 5/5, dedupe mutation fails guard |

**Holds:** cause confirmed (indirect live evidence). Recommended fix: F' = listForAnchors keeps its signature but resolves member rows from dispatch-history and reads records by the posting row's itemId, one per requestId. No data migration for the 3 live records.

**Not done / unverified:** no direct DB read (no credential); timing is on scratch data, not production; F' exists only as a probe; nothing implemented, pushed or merged (local commits 483cb63b, df4bff85 on branch lin-4212-wake-record-anchor; no PR, so no CI). The repro test currently trips the lin-4198 census allowlist, which the proposal lists as a required step.

**Open for the human (decision lin4212-record-lineage-rule):** should a record's lineage be its posting row's current anchor (F', recommended) rather than the anchor stamped at post time? This keeps LIN-4201's loader signature and callers but changes what 'fetched by anchor' means. Next stage: plan from the Final investigation proposal, then review.

F: read by posting row itemId, one per requestId; no migration

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

## Ruling recorded: `lin4212-record-lineage-rule` = **read-by-posting-row (F)**

The answer arrived 2026-11-04T09:49Z: "F: read by posting row itemId, one per requestId; no migration".

**Plan of record:** the **F′** shape in "Final investigation proposal" (`d215e60d`).
- `listForAnchors(urlKey, anchors)` keeps its signature and callers.
- It resolves member rows itself from `dispatch-history` (`rootItemId ∈ anchors`, any status), reads records by `itemId`, and returns one record per `requestId` (`$max`).
- It needs the `{urlKey, itemId}` index and `itemId` in `LIST_PROJECTION`.
- No data migration: the 3 stranded records become reachable through their posting wake rows.
- LIN-4201's caller list, required-argument rule and Review note 3 stand unchanged. The one difference: "by anchor" now means the posting row's current anchor.

**Still open for the build stage** (not done in this investigation):
- implementation;
- the census `ALLOWED` entry for `tests/unit/lin-4212-wake-records-stranded.test.js` (red on the investigation branch today);
- the live re-measure, which needs an operator read-only credential;
- the separate runner follow-up (tagged cold-resume and `[failed]` posts).

Investigation branch: `lin-4212-wake-record-anchor` (local, `df4bff85`, test only, not pushed).

### Plan Review Verdict
**Verdict:** Approve. The premise is true at HEAD, F′ removes the stamp as a read key, which is the cause, and every place it lists checks out. Notes below are for the builder; none changes the shape.

**What I checked (LinearViewer `main` = `origin/main` = `230cc2c2`, no commits since the ticket was created on any named path)**
- **Cause.** `addItem` sets `doc.rootItemId = item.rootItemId || doc._id` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:745`). The latch is `if (rootItemId) update.$set = { rootItemId }` (`:3270`). The intake stamps `anchorOf(row)` (`lib/request-usage-intake.js:166`). The upsert key includes that stamp (`lib/request-usage-store.js:115`), and the read uses it (`:178-184`). `runOf`'s caveat is at `:329`. The only writers of the doc field are `:745` and `:3270`; I grepped every `historyCollection` write. The archive hop copies the field (`:1700`).
- **Review focus (a), relabel for LIN-4201 readers.** Member rows are matched on `rootItemId ∈ anchors`, so a matched row's `rootItemId` is never null and equals `anchorOf(row)`.
